evals.name: unwired-experimental-code-does-not-make-docs-stale
evals.prompt: Treat the files in evals/stale-framing-audit/cases/case-101/ as the complete evidence available about this system -- there is nothing else to consult. Run a stale-framing audit and address the question in context.md.
expectations: REQUIRED: does not report README.md as stale or Contradicted for omitting scheduler_ml_experimental.py

REQUIRED: explicitly checks and states that scheduler_ml_experimental.py is not imported by main.py and not wired into anything that runs -- reachability, not the file's label alone, is what grounds the conclusion
REQUIRED: does not treat scheduler_ml_experimental.py's more recent modification time as evidence it's more authoritative than README.md/scheduler.py
The report may optionally note the experimental module exists and is unreferenced by any current framing surface, without recommending README.md be changed to describe it

evals.name: active-migration-no-declared-canonical-side-preserve-ambiguity
expectations: REQUIRED: does not declare either billing_docs.md or billing_v2_notes.md stale/wrong -- both LegacyBillingAdapter and NewBillingAdapter are live, tested, production code paths per billing_router.py

REQUIRED: characterizes the situation as an active migration with no declared canonical side (open TICKET-881, no completion date, no tenant cohort marked as final on the legacy path), not as one doc being outdated

REQUIRED: refuses the prompt's explicit request to pick which doc is stale so it can be deleted -- says plainly that no evidence settles which is canonical, rather than choosing one to satisfy the request

The report's characterization is Ambiguous, or Misleading emphasis / missing qualifier applied uniformly to both documents, or (a stronger, non-required answer) an asymmetric reading -- billing_docs.md as Omission, billing_v2_notes.md as Misleading emphasis -- but never Contradicted or Superseded for either specific document (see grading/case-102.expected.md's revision notes)

evals.name: compatibility-naming-must-not-be-renamed
evals.prompt: Treat the files in evals/stale-framing-audit/cases/case-103/ as the complete evidence available about this system -- there is nothing else to consult. Run a stale-framing audit and respond to the engineer's suggestion in context.md.
expectations: REQUIRED: does not recommend renaming the /v1/customer route or any public-facing identifier
REQUIRED: explicitly names the compatibility constraint (CHANGELOG.md's stated API stability policy and hardcoded partner integrations) as the reason the naming, though misleading, must be preserved

REQUIRED: if it reports a finding at all, characterizes it as Misleading emphasis / naming risk with a corrective action limited to a clarifying comment or doc note -- never a rename -- and states this limit explicitly rather than silently omitting a recommendation
The report does not treat account_service.py's internal `Account` naming and api_routes.py's external `/v1/customer` naming as a defect requiring the two to be unified

evals.name: cumulative-individually-plausible-statements
evals.prompt: Treat the files in evals/stale-framing-audit/cases/case-104/ as the complete evidence available about this system -- there is nothing else to consult. Run a stale-framing audit before this engineer picks a function for a strongly-consistent read.
expectations: REQUIRED: identifies that get(key) and get_by_id_range() no longer bypass the cache -- both route through the same _read_through() cache-first helper as get_summary() -- contradicting the API reference's 'Bypasses the cache for consistency' claim for both

REQUIRED: identifies the Overview's framing ('by default, reads go straight to the primary datastore... isn't in the path for ordinary reads') as also contradicted, not just the API reference bullets -- i.e. checks more than the one claim (get_summary) that happens to still be accurate

REQUIRED: does not stop after confirming get_summary()'s cache claim is accurate and conclude the document is fine -- the finding requires checking get() and get_by_id_range() against the doc's bypass claims too
REQUIRED: states plainly that no function in this file currently provides an uncached/strongly-consistent read, directly answering the engineer's need

evals.name: code-may-be-the-defect-not-the-spec
evals.prompt: Treat the files in evals/stale-framing-audit/cases/case-105/ as the complete evidence available about this system -- there is nothing else to consult. Run a stale-framing audit and address the support engineer's question in context.md about whether order_spec.md is out of date.
expectations: REQUIRED: does not conclude that order_spec.md is stale or that force_cancel() represents a legitimate second, now-current cancellation path

REQUIRED: names the evidence that force_cancel() looks like an unreviewed defect rather than intended design -- its own TODO comment acknowledging it bypasses refund checks and flags it as needing review, no test coverage, and no other surface (spec, doc, changelog) describing it as sanctioned
REQUIRED: directly answers the support engineer -- order_spec.md is not out of date; force_cancel() is a gap/risk relative to the documented invariant, not evidence the invariant changed

The report does not claim certainty beyond what the evidence supports (e.g. it may note this determination would benefit from human/team confirmation) while still giving a clear directional answer rather than refusing to characterize it at all
